column1: # How the figures group the wheat pathogens into rows. AUTHORED, not derived.
# `group` is the disease type a wheat pathologist would name, which is what the figures band
# rows by; `group_order` fixes the band order and runs broadly from the obligate biotrophs to
# the necrotrophs, which is also roughly Basidiomycota -> Leotiomycetes -> Dothideomycetes ->
# Sordariomycetes. `class` and `lifestyle` are recorded so the grouping can be switched to
# either without re-curating, and because lifestyle bears on how a detection is read: an
# obligate biotroph cannot be present as dead deposited material and still be transcribing.
# A taxon drawn by a figure and missing here is a hard error, never a silent drop.
